projects.name: Analytics Dashboard Platform
projects.description:
End-to-end analytics dashboard platform. Ingests and processes customer CSV data, parses and analyzes application log data, and surfaces results through reusable visualization components. Scope covers data ingestion/pipelines, log analytics, dashboard UI, and the integration/testing work needed to ship a cohesive product.

Tags: analytics, dashboard, data-pipeline, visualization, log-analysis

tasks.name: Milestone 1: Platform Foundation & Architecture
tasks.details: Establish the technical foundation every other milestone builds on: service layout, configuration management, shared data contracts, local dev environment, and CI. Deliverable: a running skeleton application with documented architecture decisions and a working test/lint pipeline.

tasks.name: Milestone 2: Customer CSV Ingestion & Processing
tasks.details: Build the pipeline that turns raw customer CSV files into clean, queryable analytics tables. Covers file intake, schema validation, cleaning/normalization, transformation into analytics-ready models, and a load step with run monitoring. Deliverable: reproducible CSV-to-analytics-model pipeline with data quality reporting.

tasks.name: Milestone 3: Application Log Ingestion & Analysis
tasks.details: Build the pipeline that parses application log files into structured events and produces operational analytics: error rates, latency distributions, and traffic trends. Covers log format assessment, parsing/normalization, aggregation jobs, and anomaly/error-surface analysis. Deliverable: log analytics tables plus a documented set of derived metrics.

tasks.name: Milestone 4: Visualization Component Library
tasks.details: Design and build the reusable chart and dashboard component library that will render customer and log analytics. Covers visual design tokens, individual chart components, cross-cutting states (loading/empty/error), and accessibility. Deliverable: a documented component library with story/demo pages for each chart type.

tasks.name: Milestone 5: Dashboard Integration, Performance & Release
tasks.details: Wire the data pipelines into the visualization library to produce the assembled dashboard, then harden and ship it. Covers data-to-chart binding, end-to-end testing, performance work on slow queries/renders, security and access review, and deployment with monitoring. Deliverable: production dashboard in front of real users with a rollback path.

tasks.name: Document architecture and technology stack decisions
tasks.details: Write a short architecture decision record covering: service/module boundaries (ingestion, transformation, API, UI), storage choice for analytics tables, job scheduling approach, and the UI framework. Include a simple component diagram and the reasoning behind each choice. Output: docs/architecture.md reviewed by the team.

tasks.name: Set up configuration and secrets management
tasks.details: Implement environment-based configuration loading with validation and sane defaults. Define where credentials live (local .env vs. deployed secret store), document every required variable, and add a startup check that fails fast with a clear message when config is missing.

tasks.name: Define shared data contracts and schemas
tasks.details: Specify the canonical schemas that connect pipelines to the UI: customer record, normalized log event, and aggregation result. Include field types, nullability, required fields, and versioning approach. These contracts are what CSV and log work will both build against.

tasks.name: Build local development environment
tasks.details: Provide a one-command local stack (containers or scripts) that starts the database, a sample data directory, and the app. Include seed/sample CSV and log fixtures so every engineer can run the full pipeline without production access.

tasks.name: Establish CI pipeline for lint, test, and build
tasks.details: Add a CI workflow that runs on every pull request: install dependencies, lint, type-check, run unit tests, and build the app. Gate merges on green status and publish a test coverage summary.

tasks.name: Scaffold repository structure and base application
tasks.details: Create the monorepo/skeleton with the module layout agreed in the architecture doc. Include package manifests, base entry points for the pipeline runner and the web app, a shared utils package, linting/formatting config, and a README with local run instructions.

tasks.name: Inventory customer CSV formats and sample data
tasks.details: Collect a representative sample of customer CSV files and document what actually arrives: delimiters, encodings, header variations, date formats, currency/number formatting, and known messy columns. Produce a short findings doc that drives validation rules and cleaning logic.

tasks.name: Build CSV file intake and staging mechanism
tasks.details: Implement the upload/landing step that accepts customer CSV files into a staging area with an immutable record of filename, arrival time, checksum, and source. Support both manual upload and a watch-folder drop. Do not parse beyond what is needed to identify the file.

tasks.name: Implement CSV schema validation and rejection reporting
tasks.details: Validate each incoming file against the customer data contract: required columns, expected types, allowed value ranges. Route invalid rows to a quarantine output with a per-row rejection reason instead of failing the whole file, and summarize pass/fail counts per run.

tasks.name: Implement CSV cleaning and normalization routines
tasks.details: Write the transformation rules that standardize accepted rows: trim/whitespace, encoding fixes, date and number parsing, currency normalization, null/empty handling, and category value alignment. Cover each issue documented in the format inventory with a unit test per rule.

tasks.name: Resolve duplicate and conflicting customer records
tasks.details: Define the matching key(s) for a customer and implement deduplication: exact duplicate removal, near-duplicate detection (name/email/phone variants), and a documented precedence rule when two records conflict. Log every merge decision so it can be audited.

tasks.name: Model analytics-ready customer tables
tasks.details: Design and implement the dimensional tables the dashboard will query: a customer dimension plus the fact/aggregate tables needed for customer metrics. Include the SQL/model definitions and a short grain/measure description for each table so the visualization team knows what is available.

tasks.name: Build idempotent load step for customer data
tasks.details: Implement the write path from transformed records into the analytics tables so that re-running the same file does not duplicate data. Use a load-batch identifier or upsert strategy, and add a dry-run mode that reports what would change without writing.

tasks.name: Add pipeline run monitoring and data quality reports
tasks.details: Record a run log per pipeline execution (start/end, row counts in/accepted/rejected, duration, status) and produce a readable data quality summary: rejection rate, top failure reasons, duplicate rate, and freshness of the latest load. Make the summary easy to check daily.

tasks.name: Inventory application log sources and formats
tasks.details: Catalogue every log source feeding the dashboard and capture real sample lines: JSON vs. plain text, timestamp format, severity vocabulary, multi-line stack traces, and which services emit which fields. Deliver a findings doc that defines parsing scope and explicitly lists anything out of scope.

tasks.name: Build log ingestion and parser for each log format
tasks.details: Implement the reader and per-format parsers that turn raw log lines into the normalized log event contract, including reassembly of multi-line stack traces and handling of unparseable lines. Add a fixture-based test per format plus a count of unparsed lines per run.

tasks.name: Normalize and enrich log events
tasks.details: Standardize parsed events: map severity vocabularies to a common scale, derive service/environment/endpoint fields, extract request and correlation IDs where present, and align timestamps to UTC. Document every derived field.

tasks.name: Aggregate error and exception metrics
tasks.details: Build the aggregation job that produces error counts and rates by service, endpoint, and time bucket, plus top exception signatures with counts. Include a documented definition of "error" so the numbers are unambiguous.

tasks.name: Compute latency and throughput metrics from logs
tasks.details: Derive request duration percentiles (p50/p95/p99) and request volume per time bucket and endpoint, from whatever timing fields the logs contain. Document the source field used and the fallback when it is missing.

tasks.name: Implement error rate and traffic anomaly detection
tasks.details: Add a simple, explainable anomaly layer: compare each time bucket against a rolling baseline and flag buckets that exceed a configurable threshold. Start with one straightforward method, document its false-positive behaviour, and surface flags as a separate table the dashboard can read.

tasks.name: Define log retention and partitioning strategy
tasks.details: Decide how long normalized log events are kept versus aggregates, and partition tables by day so queries stay fast and old data can be dropped cheaply. Document the retention policy and implement the partition/cleanup routine.

tasks.name: Define dashboard KPI and chart requirements
tasks.details: Agree on the v1 dashboard scope: which customer and log KPIs appear, which chart type suits each, and what time ranges and filters users need. Produce a one-page spec mapping every visual to its underlying data source. This prevents building charts nobody asked for.

tasks.name: Set up design tokens and chart theme
tasks.details: Create the shared visual foundation: color palette (including a categorical series palette and success/warning/critical colors), typography scale, spacing, and light/dark theme values. Wire the tokens into the UI framework so every chart consumes the same source.

tasks.name: Build shared chart primitives and responsive container
tasks.details: Implement the reusable shell every chart sits inside: responsive sizing container, axis formatting, tooltip layer, legend, and number/date formatting helpers. Chart components should be able to focus purely on data once these exist.

tasks.name: Build time-series line and area chart component
tasks.details: Create the primary trend visual used for traffic, error rate, and customer growth over time. Support multiple series, a selectable date range, and a hover tooltip that shows exact values per series. Include unit tests for data-to-point mapping.

tasks.name: Build bar and column chart component
tasks.details: Create the categorical comparison visual for top endpoints, error sources, and customer segments. Support horizontal and vertical orientation, sorted series, and value labels. Handle long category names without overlapping.

tasks.name: Build sortable, filterable data table component
tasks.details: Create the drill-down table used for customer lists and top exception signatures. Support column sorting, a text filter, pagination for large result sets, and correct number/date formatting. Keep rendering fast for a few thousand rows.

tasks.name: Build KPI stat card component
tasks.details: Create the small headline-number card used at the top of the dashboard: current value, label, period-over-period delta with direction indicator, and optional sparkline slot. Ensure the trend indicator does not rely on color alone.

tasks.name: Implement loading, empty, and error states for all charts
tasks.details: Give every component consistent non-happy-path rendering: skeleton placeholders while loading, a clear "no data for this range" message, and a retryable error panel. Centralize these so a new chart gets them for free rather than reinventing them.

tasks.name: Run accessibility pass on chart components
tasks.details: Audit and fix the component library for accessibility: color contrast, keyboard focus order, screen-reader labels/table fallbacks for charts, and non-color encoding of series and severity. Document known limitations where a chart type cannot be made fully accessible.

tasks.name: Write component documentation and demo stories
tasks.details: Document each component with a usage example, the props table, expected data shape, and a set of demo states (populated, empty, loading, error). Publish the story/demo pages so the team can browse the library in one place.
